lines: A race doesn't always run from Go to the line. You might pause, leave, lose the bike, or win.
Against bots, the bar has Leave. Solo, it has Pause and End. Either way out opens Race Setup at once, with no confirmation, and earns no XP.
Only a solo race pauses. The clock, the distance and the standings hold, and the card blocks none of the buttons.
Resume carries the race on. So does pedalling again, once you have stopped, so the stroke under your press never undoes it.
If the bike stops answering, an alert says so with Reconnect. You coast, your speed falling to a stop over fifteen seconds, the resistance buttons off.
Back in time, the race carries on. Fifteen seconds without the bike, and the race ends as a DNF, never a silent stop, with a way back to Race Setup.
Solo, nobody else is on your clock, so the race parks until the bike is back, then carries on from where it stopped.
The line is the map's distance. Cross it, and your finish time is the race clock, your place is where you crossed, and Results opens.
Pause works the same from a phone to a desktop, its button forty-eight pixels under your thumb.
What the tests prove: eleven new behaviour specs, the coast and the finish line in unit tests, all green, and the first bundle unchanged.
Telo Ride, from the Telo family, turns a smart bike at home into a game.
It pairs with the bike over Bluetooth, reads your power and sets resistance for every hill and interval.

lines.text: Two doors: Race, ride a map against your best-time ghost, bots or people; and Classes, ride along to a video, alone or with a group; fed by one progression of XP, rider levels, stars and map unlocks.
